australian_locale_opacity: On the Australian locale the same speech produced three weak positions, two of them inside the word car, but the locale returns no phone names, so what the scorer believed was said cannot be recovered. This is the practical cost of a score only lane.
confounds: the performed American pass was read markedly more slowly, up to two and a half times the duration of the same sentence in the Australian pass, so it is a naturalness confound and not an American reference
the performed American pass scored worse than the natural Australian pass almost everywhere, which is consistent with careful unnatural reading rather than with accent
no production in either pass carries an expert human label, so no phone here is known to be correct or incorrect
one speaker, one session, one room, one microphone
control_sentence_caveat: The control sentence contains no dental fricatives, so it avoids TH fronting by accident rather than by design. Fricatives are not a dialect stable class and no such class list exists in ASHA or Speech Pathology Australia guidance.

excluded_sentence_ids.s4: the American pass said skew jewel instead of schedule, so the words differ
excluded_sentence_ids.s6: the Australian pass omitted the word to, so the words differ
excluded_sentence_ids.s8: a control sentence, not read at all in the American pass

design.reference_text: identical for both passes; the respelling in the script was a reading aid only

predeclared_divergence_points.l: dark l is commonly vocalised in Australian English, as in table
predeclared_divergence_points.t: Australian final and pre pausal t is commonly glottalised or unreleased
predeclared_divergence_points.æ: the BATH and TRAP split; Australian uses a long a in class and dance
predeclared_divergence_points.ɔɹ: r coloured vowel; Australian English is non rhotic
predeclared_divergence_points.ɚ: r coloured vowel; Australian English is non rhotic
predeclared_divergence_points.ɹ: post vocalic r; Australian English is non rhotic

headline_finding.statement: Natural Australian speech scored on the General American model produced ten phones below 80. Nine of the ten fall on divergence points written down before the scores were read. None fell on the dialect stable control sentence.

sentence_score_masking: Utterance level accuracy for the same clips sat between 95 and 99, so the sentence score showed nothing while the phone level marked Australian features as errors. Any work that reads only an overall score would miss this entirely.
what_this_cannot_do: It cannot estimate Australian performance, cannot separate an Australian feature from a genuine production difficulty at any single point, cannot select a system, cannot set or move a threshold, and cannot enter any gate calculation.
what_this_changes: Initially read as qualifying the locality argument. That reading was too confident and is corrected: with one speaker and no induced errors, a clean control sentence is equally consistent with those phones being dialect stable and with this speaker simply articulating them well, and no base rate exists for how often an ordinary speaker falls below threshold. Locality remains untested in both directions. The coverage, magnitude and direction arguments are untouched and remain binding.
